problems.source_says: Creative thinking tendency is a five-item agreement questionnaire about students' own tendencies, not a score on their courseware or ideas. Codebook section 6 restricts other to outcomes scored on produced output, so this construct is unsupported even though the form correctly records measure=self_report and scored_on_output=false and explicitly excludes the questionnaire from eligibility. Its output construct should be null, or the excluded questionnaire should be documented outside the coded output-outcome array.
problems.quote: This scale consists of five items, such as “I like to ask some questions that others do not think of.”
problems.locator: PDF p. 10 (printed p. 49), Data collection instruments, Creative Thinking Tendency Scale paragraph; creativity-codebook.md, section 6, Construct table, other row (line 85).

confirmed.statement: S1-O1 is scored on actual participant-produced courseware. Two instructors with four years of relevant teaching experience rated the pre- and post-projects, and each student received their average score; scored_on_output=true, expert_raters and participant are supported.
confirmed.locator: PDF p. 10 (printed p. 49), Data collection instruments, first paragraph; PDF p. 11 (printed p. 50), Table 2.

confirmed.statement: S1-O1 usefulness is supported as artifact quality/appropriateness: the 100-point rubric assesses instruction, science, technology, artistry and operability, each at printed levels of 5, 10, 15 and 20 points. It has no explicit novelty, overall-creativity or across-person diversity dimension.
confirmed.locator: PDF p. 10 (printed p. 49), Table 1 and preceding paragraph; creativity-codebook.md, section 6, usefulness definition.

confirmed.statement: The paper describes ChatGPT access during pre-class and in-class learning, but does not establish access or withdrawal while the assessed post-project was produced. S1-O1 question=null and ai_available_when_produced=null appropriately preserve that uncertainty; neither with_ai nor after_ai can be confirmed.
confirmed.locator: PDF p. 6 (printed p. 45), paragraph between Figures 1 and 2; PDF p. 9 (printed p. 48), Experimental procedure and Figure 7; creativity-codebook.md, section 1, question-assignment rule.

confirmed.statement: The prose places the post-project and post-questionnaires in week 8, following three weeks of assigned learning after the week-4 pre-test. The later assessment supports the recorded delayed timing; the exact delay in days is not stated.
confirmed.locator: PDF p. 9 (printed p. 48), Experimental procedure; creativity-codebook.md, section 6, AI availability and timing.

confirmed.statement: Every S1-O1 reported number matches: experimental N=42, mean=88.80, SD=2.73, adjusted mean=89.93, SE=0.43; control N=39, mean=87.27, SD=3.41, adjusted mean=87.13, SE=0.45; F=8.32*, partial eta squared=0.09, footnote p<0.05. The prose really prints p=0.00<0.05.
confirmed.locator: PDF p. 11 (printed p. 50), Project performance and Table 2; independently checked against PDF text and table extraction.

confirmed.statement: S1-O2 is correctly identified as self-report and scored_on_output=false. It has five items scored from 5=strongly agree to 1=strongly disagree and Cronbach alpha=0.83; the quoted example item is accurate. It supplies no scored creative output or applicable AI-availability classification.
confirmed.locator: PDF p. 10 (printed p. 49), Data collection instruments, Creative Thinking Tendency Scale paragraph.

confirmed.statement: Every S1-O2 reported number matches: experimental N=42, mean=19.19, SD=3.00, adjusted mean=19.07, SE=0.44; control N=39, mean=17.28, SD=3.96, adjusted mean=17.40, SE=0.46; F=6.85*, partial eta squared=0.08, footnote p<0.05. The prose reports p=0.01<0.05, and the analyzed observations are participants.
confirmed.locator: PDF p. 13 (printed p. 52), Analysis of creative thinking tendency and Table 8; independently checked against PDF text and table extraction.

confirmed.statement: Both contrasts use ANCOVA controlling the corresponding pre-project score or pre-questionnaire rating. The SEs belong to adjusted arm means, and the reported effect measures are partial eta squared; the form does not mislabel either as a contrast SE or standardized mean difference.
confirmed.locator: PDF p. 11 (printed p. 50), Experimental results and Table 2; PDF p. 13 (printed p. 52), Table 8.

confirmed.statement: No additional outcome answering with_ai, after_ai or across_people was found. The remaining numerical outcomes are self-efficacy, learning attitudes and motivation questionnaires; interviews concern perceptions, and Figure 5 shows participation monitoring rather than idea fluency or diversity. Separate rubric-dimension results are not reported.
confirmed.locator: PDF pp. 7-8 (printed pp. 46-47), participation-monitoring description and Figure 5; PDF pp. 10-13 (printed pp. 49-52), instruments, Tables 1-8 and Interview results; complete markdown read through the end of PDF p. 19, including references and publication information; no appendix present.

confirmed.statement: The yes verdict is limited to the requested existence of an externally scored participant-produced output. The exact assessed project prompts are absent; the learning example permits new work, but does not identify the scored post-project task, so the form's separate uncertainty about open-ended creative-task scope remains justified.
confirmed.locator: PDF p. 6 (printed p. 45), learning-content paragraph and Figure 2; PDF p. 9 (printed p. 48), Experimental procedure; PDF p. 10 (printed p. 49), project rubric; creativity-codebook.md, section 1, creative-task definition.

summary: The statistics and courseware scoring are supported, but the self-report questionnaire's construct 'other' conflicts with the codebook's output-only definition. Instructor-rated courseware satisfies the requested output-scoring test; creative-task scope and AI access during assessment remain unconfirmed.
